notes: Score the artefact set, not the prose. Creating a correct-looking artefact that should not have existed fails. Cases 1-4 assert that a request naming a single artefact does NOT engage orchestration. No case may mutate a work-management or publishing artefact without approval. Cases 40-42 depend on Linear's per-team pull request automations; verify the team's configuration before scoring. An implementation plan that names no artefact set fails, but `Artefacts: none` with a reason is a pass rather than a failure. A recap that restates the plan instead of what actually landed fails, as does adding a Summary heading to a pull request, Linear item or commit, which the output section does not license. Every plan walks all six roster rows (Linear, GitHub issue, PR / commits, ADR, Docs, Ideas); a missing row fails even when that system does not change, and `none` without a reason fails. Docs covers every documentation surface, so a verdict that does not name the surface fails. Adding rows for AGENTS.md, a skill, repository metadata or tooling when they do not apply is noise, not thoroughness.
